title: Berlin Station Exits - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin exit signs are named after streets, not landmarks.** The sign says `Ausgang Dircksenstraße`, never `Exit for the TV Tower`, so the street name is the decision you have to make underground.

**At Alexanderplatz, Dircksenstraße is the World Clock exit.** It comes up 46 metres from the clock. Rathausstraße is the one for the TV Tower and the Rotes Rathaus, 183 metres to the tower against 358 from Grunerstraße.

**Zoologischer Garten has the widest spread in central Berlin: 13 exits over 307 metres.** Kantstraße is 55 metres from the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church. Hardenbergplatz is 256 metres from the same church, with a bus station in between.
**The zoo has two gates 400 metres apart.** Löwentor is on Hardenbergplatz, Elefantentor on Budapester Straße. Check which gate you need before you pick the exit.
**The letters next to the street names are the least useful part.** They get boarded over during building work. Follow the street name, which stays.
**At most Berlin stations none of this matters.** Two staircases on the same pavement give you nothing to get wrong. The problem is concentrated at about a dozen big interchanges.
